newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends down as frost fears subside.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends down as frost fears subside.

text.p: CSCE coffee posted moderate losses on Wednesday, pressured by an absence of damaging cold in Brazil and signs of a build-up in U.S. stockpiles, traders said.
Benchmark September futures fell 2.90 cents a lb on the day, to 172.35 cents. The market hovered within a narrow range throughout the thinly-traded session, posting trades from 170 to 175 cents.
Concern that a cold airmass moving into southern Brazil over the weekend could threaten Brazil's coffee crop sparked a round of nervous buying early in the week.
But the buying interest began to wane by late yesterday after a round of forecasts predicted mild winter weather for the world's biggest coffee grower.

The sell-off continued this morning, as meteorologists confirmed a frost-free outlook for the next week. Scale-down roaster buying helped cushion the slide, dealers said, preventing a test of support in the 169-167 cent area basis September.
News that some 27,000 bags of coffee were delivered on Tuesday to exchange-certified warehouses also weighed on prices.
While the coffee still needs to pass grading to be certified for delivery against CSCE futures, dealers said its appearance was enough to drive prices lower this morning.
"It's a substantial amount of coffee compared to what has been offered before," said one trader.

"On the other hand, it's not enough to cover the open interest in the futures," he added. The spot July contract, which expires in three weeks, had 703 lots open interest as of July 1, equal to about 200,000 bags of coffee.
After the close of business on Wednesday, the CSCE reported an additional 55,000 bags were awaiting grading in exchange warehouses, bringing the total pending cache to 82,000 bags.
With many traders already absent ahead of the U.S. long weekend, the day's turnover was scant, at 3,757 lots. The CSCE will be closed on Friday, July 4, for the Independence Day holiday.
